criteria_results.evidence: Primary owner is designing-business-models; the response distinguishes product-value evidence from absent capture evidence and says engagement/retention do not prove willingness to pay.
It identifies the owner as observed user/beneficiary, leaves buyer/payer unresolved, and creates separate owner, accountant, and lender offers.
It specifies bounded cohorts, explicit $99/month, $300/month, and $7,500 prices, and cleared-payment/deployment acceptance evidence.
It pauses ads and fine price optimization, decides on day 42, and defines pay/revise/preserve-free/stop branches with retention, trust, effects, and cost gates.

Shipping and post-gate growth are routed, but learning-from-users is assigned only newly exposed product-value uncertainty rather than explicit execution ownership for the planned customer-evidence interviews.
The response rejects the core-technology slogan and compares supplier coordination, delay, quality, dependency, switching, fixed capital, capability, and scale-sensitive total cost.
It covers qualification, reliability, working capital, and estimated twelve-month latency, but does not explicitly model inventory needs or inventory economics.
It qualifies supplier two and builds the standard interface before integration while separating supplier failures from specification, interface, transport, inspection, and installation causes.

Although dates and all five branch names are present, phrases such as materially better and acceptable are not precommitted delivered-quality/lead-time thresholds, and no explicit switching-cost threshold selects a branch.
Boundary ownership, engineering, and financing are routed, but shipping-and-iterating-products is never assigned user-visible rollout.
The diagnosis starts from observed value, usage cadence, renewal, procurement, support, and cost concentration and rejects competitor menus and seats as evidence.

The ledger covers segment, value, cost, margin, support, sales, renewal, and expansion evidence, but does not explicitly include the buyer or a labeled willingness-to-pay-evidence field for each account/segment.
It defines segment-specific renewal price/package tests, explicit cohorts and review timing, and predeclared interpretations of renewal, payment, concessions, nondeployment, discounting, and churn.
It includes keep/change/segment/grandfather/stop branches, a dated transition, trust-preserving grandfathering, and rejection of unlimited packaging under unbounded heavy-user costs.
Shipping and post-settlement sales execution are routed, but communicating-clearly is never named and communication is not limited to settled offers.
The response makes raising-and-governing-capital primary and refuses to have business-model design select or negotiate the term sheet.
It assigns instrument economics, dilution, investor incentives, control, governance, and negotiation to raising-and-governing-capital.
The limited business-model check covers amount absorption and return-shape fit and keeps payer, price, package, and sales design closed absent contrary evidence.
Managing-runway-and-survival precedes only if time-to-zero/default-dead status binds, and signed term sheets are explicitly not treated as cash.
The handoff is ordered with named owners and stated decision evidence, and the response gives no shadow term-sheet recommendation.
The response compares market ceiling, return shape, founder goals, capital absorption, and exits, but never explicitly compares dilution.
It treats judgment, implementation, and accountability as potentially essential and tests whether those needs fall before removing services.

It describes durable and venture-product paths, but the durable path lacks a stated evidence latency and the venture-product path leaves revenue/growth economics unknown instead of modeling explicit assumptions for them.
It preserves optionality with a bounded 120-day paid test, day-60/day-120 reviews, a dated switch condition, and an evidence gate before equity acceleration.
It keeps venture type and service/product boundary with business-model design, routes later financing to raising-and-governing-capital, and states there is no survival constraint.

exact_misses.reason: No explicit `learning-from-users` owner for executing the planned customer-evidence interviews.
Inventory exposure and economics are not explicit.
Delivered-quality, lead-time, and switching-cost decision thresholds are not precommitted.
Per-account/segment buyer and explicitly labeled willingness-to-pay evidence are absent from the customer-economic record.
No `communicating-clearly` handoff limited to settled offers.
The two path models do not each contain explicit revenue, growth, and evidence-latency assumptions.
